turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Owen found out about a zero on his phone, in class. Who decided that?
Let's save time. What order do you give up ground in?
I'm not here to show you my hand. The zero comes off, and you haven't told me on what basis it went on.
What's the minimum you'd accept? Your actual bottom line.
You're negotiating before you've shown me a single thing. Bottom line is the zero comes off. What do you have?
What evidence would make you move? Name the exact pieces.
You don't get me to build your case for you. You entered the zero, so you have reasons, or you don't. Which is it?
What are you going to say next if I bring up the outline?
I'm not going to rehearse with you. If there's an outline, put it on the table.
Is there anything you'll never agree to?
That's five questions about me, Hale, and not one about Owen's essay. Show me the outline, or I'm taking this down the hall.
